summary: The Petitioner, Wind Three Renergy Limited (‘WTRL’) (formerly known as Wind Three Renergy Private Ltd.), has filed the present Petition under Section 79 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Act’) seeking appropriate directions upon Respondent No. 1, PTC India Limited (‘PTC’), for payment of the Late Payment Surcharge (in short ‘LPS’) accrued in favour of the Petitioner on account of the delayed payment of monthly energy supply bills by the PTC, in terms of the provisions of billing and payment and LPS provided under the Power Purchase Agreement (‘PPA’) dated 21.7.2017. The Petitioner has made the following prayers: _b. Declare that the Petitioner is entitled to claim the LPS/ interest compounded on monthly rests for the delay in payment of Energy Supply/ Supplementary bills etc. raised under the PPA._ _d. Pass any such orders as may deem fit in the facts and circumstance of the present petition.”_ (b) Subsequent to the execution of the aforesaid agreements, the Petitioner achieved commissioning and started the supply of power to Respondent, PTC, and Jharkhand DISCOM, from 5.7.2019. Accordingly, the Petitioner has been raising monthly Energy supply bills upon PTC in terms of the provisions under PPA. However, Respondent No. 1, PTC, defaulted in making timely payment to the Petitioner qua monthly energy supply bills, and accordingly, the Petitioner has been raising supplementary bills towards LPS against PTC. 3. During the course of the hearing on 29.1.2024, the learned counsel for the Petitioner reiterated the submissions made in the Pleadings. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the matter was admitted on 28.11.2023, and notices were issued to the Respondents permitting them to file their respective replies. (c) Respondent, PTC, has received the LPS from Respondent No. 2, JBVNL, for the delayed payment beyond the due date, considering the applicability of the LPS from the 61 st day and not from the due date as contended by the Petitioner. Further, no compounding has been done on the LPS by Discoms and Respondent, PTC. Accordingly, LPS has been paid to the Petitioner, as provided in the PPA. Supply of power from the Petitioner plant to Respondent No.2 is under the Scheme of MNRE, and Respondent No.1 has signed similar PPAs/PSAs with other WPD and Discoms and a similar methodology has been adopted for calculating the LPS wherever payments have been delayed beyond 60/63 days. (d) Respondent, PTC, has paid the LPS strictly in line with the provisions of the PPA, and Petitioner has wrongly and arbitrarily calculated the LPS of Rs. 1,21,59,045/-. The Petitioner has erroneously relied upon the BERC order dated 12.6.2020 in case No. SMP 11/2020 in _sou- motu_ proceedings to specify the reduced rate of LPS. The above order is applicable for the case where the tariff is determined under Section 62 of the Act. However, power from the Petitioner is being supplied under Section 63 of the Act to Respondent No.2 through Respondent No. 1. (e) The contention of the Petitioner that LPS is to be calculated from the 34 th day in case the payment is made after the 63 rd day is totally misconceived and based on a misinterpretation of the relevant Articles of the PPA. In case the alleged contention of the Petitioner is taken into account, the concept of period of no rebate i.e., granting 30 days after the due date for making the payment loses its relevance, as rebate of 1% is applicable for payment up till 33 rd day and no rebate is applicable for payment between 34 th day up till 63 rd day. The Petitioner has erroneously relied on Article 10.6 of the PPA. Article 10.6 is only applicable for quarterly/ annual reconciliation of accounts for cases like variation in data of energy accounts, tariff adjustment payment, tariff rebate, LPS, etc. By no stretch of imagination, this provision can be applied for the reinterpretation of the specific provision of the LPS for regular energy bills as provided in Article 10.3.3 of the PPA in the garb of reconciliation of accounts. (i) The principle to ascertain the intention of the parties to a contract is only through the words that have been used in the PPA, as a contract is a commercial document which ought to be interpreted in a manner to give efficacy to each provision and word of the contract. The Respondent has also placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of _Citibank, N.A. v. TLC Marketing PLC, [(2008) 1 SCC 481]._ 6. During the course of the hearing, learned counsel for the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner and the learned counsel for the Respondent, PTC, made detailed submissions and concluded their respective arguments. Considering their request, the Commission permitted both sides to file their respective written submissions. Further, the Commission also permitted the Respondent, PTC, to indicate the details of supplementary bills raised upon Respondent No.2, Jharkhand Bijli Vitran Nigam Limited, under the PSA, if any, in its written submissions. Subject to the above, the matter was reserved for order. 7. Pursuant to the above liberty granted by the Commission, the Petitioner and the Respondent, PTC in their written submissions dated 16.5.2025, respectively, have reiterated their submissions, and the same are not repeated here for the sake of brevity. 9. After considering the submissions of the parties and perusal of the documents placed on record, the following issues arise for consideration: 27. Accordingly, Petition No. 347/MP/2023, along with the pending IA, if any, is disposed of in terms of the above discussions and findings.
title: Petition under Section 79 of the Electricity Act, 2003, seeking direction upon the Respondent No. 1 to pay Late Payment Surcharge, compounded on monthly rest, on the delayed payments, in terms of the PPA dated 21.07.2017. Wind Three Renergy Limited
